# 视觉图志 · Visual Atlas

> A living atlas of human visual culture: an online museum + encyclopedia + knowledge graph covering art history, architecture, design, craft, photography, film, animation, games, digital art, fashion, industrial design, visual culture and creative science. Knowledge is always free; products sell saved time; support is by donation; ads are optional.

Content is maintained as code (git commit → build → GitHub Pages). Factual artwork images are sourced from Wikimedia Commons and their owning institutions; text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

## Main sections

- [Gallery — works, buildings, objects](https://duguboss.github.io/Art-Gallery/#/gallery): salon-style wall of 20+ analyzed works incl. Michelangelo’s David, Mona Lisa, The Last Supper, The Starry Night, The Great Wave off Kanagawa, the Parthenon, Villa Savoye, Fallingwater, Bauhaus Dessau, Katsura Imperial Villa.
- [Knowledge Atlas — 14 domains](https://duguboss.github.io/Art-Gallery/#/knowledge): domain registry plus concepts, materials and techniques indexes.
- [Explore — timeline / map / periods / cultures](https://duguboss.github.io/Art-Gallery/#/explore): four dimensions over the same graph.
- [Styles — movements & contemporary creator styles](https://duguboss.github.io/Art-Gallery/#/styles): 14 historical movements and 11 contemporary styles, each linked to its roots.
- [Artists — artists & architects](https://duguboss.github.io/Art-Gallery/#/artists): 13 people who changed visual language.
- [Learn — museum-style lessons](https://duguboss.github.io/Art-Gallery/#/learn): visual foundations (color, composition, form, space, light, material, typography, rhythm, narrative), art history, creative disciplines.
- [Practice — hands-on exercises](https://duguboss.github.io/Art-Gallery/#/practice): observation, constraint, comparison, color, cross-style AI labs.
- [Exhibitions — curated graph walks](https://duguboss.github.io/Art-Gallery/#/exhibition/geometry-from-david-to-the-interface): "The Geometry Thread", "Light Travels", "The Neighborhood of David".

## Entity model

Entities: domains, periods, cultures, places, materials, techniques, concepts, movements/styles, people, works/buildings/objects, lessons, exercises, products, exhibitions. Relations (created_by, influenced_by, emerged_from, uses_material, uses_technique, located_in, associated_with, …) are first-class edges traversable in both directions. Every work carries discipline-specific analysis blocks (painting: composition → color → light → brushwork; architecture: site → plan → structure → light).
